propositions: On platforms without /proc, _process_start_time returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing unbounded lock wedging when a dead holder's pid is recycled by an unrelated live process

The fix applies _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling to the live-pid branch only when current_start is unavailable, bounding the wedge to 1 hour while preserving the invariant that genuinely live owners holding an fcntl leg cannot be reclaimed
The owner-identity and staleness cluster was extracted from lock.py into lock_owner.py to stay within the 800-line module size limit, with all 54 references repointed and no re-export shim
A recycled pid on a no-/proc platform is now reclaimed once past the ceiling instead of wedging indefinitely, while corroborated live owners (matching start times) are never reclaimed on a timer
